blocks.text: For SFO–Bangkok on January 15, the main choice is whether you’d rather reach Bangkok on January 16 or take the quickest of the direct-award schedules that arrive January 17. The award quotes below are dated observations, not live availability. The cash search is a separate end-to-end baseline, not an award option or a confirmed party total.

If an earlier arrival matters most, the Singapore Airlines itinerary gets you in at 10:25 p.m. on January 16. It leaves SFO at 11:45 a.m. January 15 and takes 19 hours 40 minutes overall. That’s the one-day-earlier arrival compared with the late-night Aeroplan option, but it means leaving SFO about 11½ hours earlier; the two journeys also quote different award programs, so their points aren’t directly comparable.
Earlier arrival, with a midday departure.
blocks.label: Arrive January 16

blocks.text: If you prefer to leave late and still minimize elapsed time among these direct awards, the 11:15 p.m. SFO departure arrives at 9:50 a.m. on January 17 in 19 hours 35 minutes. It is five minutes quicker than the January 16-arrival itinerary in elapsed time, but arrives the next local date. Its 65,000 Aeroplan points match the other late-night Aeroplan option below; that option arrives 45 minutes later, so it adds little unless its schedule suits you better.

There is also a more complicated way to arrive before either of those January 17 schedules: the Turkish economy award via LAX is listed at 110,000 Turkish points, departing SFO at 7:00 a.m. January 15 and reaching Bangkok at 8:50 a.m. January 17. That is an earlier arrival than the late-night Aeroplan itinerary, but requires a much earlier start and a separate positioning flight to LAX. Its cash quote is for the SFO–LAX positioning leg only, not the whole trip.
Earlier January 17 arrival via separate tickets.
blocks.label: Via LAX, economy

blocks.text: A business-class Turkish award on the same reported January 15, 7:00 a.m.–January 17, 8:50 a.m. schedule is a notable alternative (J45), but it costs 275,000 Turkish points rather than 110,000 for the economy choice. Since the economy option already matches that schedule, the cabin upgrade—not an arrival-time gain—is the reason to consider spending the extra points.
The requested-route cash search found this SFO–Bangkok fare; treat it as a separate baseline, not a guaranteed party price.

Important limits: the direct Aeroplan award quotes have unknown price scope and do not establish an all-in party total. For the LAX choices, award taxes are unknown, the award price scope is unknown, and the positioning cash amount’s scope is also unknown; the one-traveler search echo does not show that it is a per-person price. The award evidence supports the requested traveler count for the direct options, but traveler-count confirmation is unknown for the separate-ticket options. The LAX itineraries are separate tickets: positioning permission, baggage and check-in arrangements, terminal or transit details, and missed-connection protection are unverified. No schedule, seat count, fare, or award should be treated as currently available or confirmed bookable.
